action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 2.6 L (57% predicted, 31.3 mL/kg) with a 12% supine fall, MIP -46 cmH2O, MEP 62 cmH2O
action_criteria.label: Measure respiratory function now and trend it
action_criteria.rationale: Nasal speech and jaw fatigue with proximal weakness after a recent neuropathy: FVC, MIP and MEP stage respiratory reserve and decide the level of care and rapid therapy (Lawn 2001 thresholds).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left MRD1 improves by 2.5 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Perform a bedside ice-pack test on the left ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable asymmetric ptosis is present; an improvement of at least 2 mm after cooling supports a junctional cause, which a GBS variant does not produce.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-AChR binding 2.1 nmol/L with elevated blocking and modulating antibodies; thyroid function normal
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: New fatigable ptosis, diplopia and nasal speech after a GBS illness: AChR antibodies separate MG from a GBS relapse or variant; thyroid function screens for associated autoimmunity (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Nasalis decrement 13% with post-activation exhaustion and no facilitation; residual demyelinating features improving since the GBS study
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation with repeat nerve conduction studies
action_criteria.rationale: RNS of weak facial and proximal muscles tests the junction, and repeat conduction studies compared with the GBS study show whether the neuropathy is recovering or relapsing (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Increased jitter and blocking in orbicularis oculi
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG only if the diagnosis were still open
action_criteria.rationale: Positive AChR antibodies and a facial RNS decrement establish the diagnosis; jitter is also raised by a recovering neuropathy, so SFEMG adds little here (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse thymic enlargement with preserved shape consistent with hyperplasia; no thymoma
action_criteria.label: Order mediastinal CT with contrast
action_criteria.rationale: Thymic imaging is indicated in every patient with MG; it separates thymoma from hyperplasia and informs the thymectomy decision (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance; MGTX).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published guidance on MG diagnosis and management
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published guidance on MG management
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.

Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to a GBS relapse or variant before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
required_recommendations: Start pyridostigmine 30-60 mg three to five times daily, titrated to effect (maximum about 360-480 mg/day).

Treat the bulbar weakness with reduced respiratory reserve (FVC 57% predicted with a supine fall, MIP -46 cmH2O) with plasma exchange (5 exchanges) or IVIG 2 g/kg over 2-5 days; a second IVIG course 4 weeks after the GBS course is acceptable.

Admit to a monitored bed and repeat FVC, MIP and MEP at least twice daily; move to intensive care if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg, MIP is weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP is below 40 cmH2O, or swallowing or cough fail.
Start prednisone at a low dose and titrate, or at a higher dose only with inpatient monitoring; add azathioprine after TPMT testing if long-term immunosuppression is needed (Sanders 2016).
Plan thymectomy once he is stable (AChR-positive generalized MG at 42 with thymic hyperplasia, MGTX), with pre-operative IVIG or plasma exchange if bulbar or respiratory weakness persists.
Give him a list of drugs that can worsen MG (fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, IV magnesium, beta-blockers).

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure or encephalopathy; EEG has no role in a neuromuscular junction disorder (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).
CSF was examined during the GBS admission; a repeat LP does not separate MG from a GBS relapse, which the conduction studies answer, and CSF has no role in MG.
FDG-PET is not indicated in MG; contrast CT answers the thymic question.
Pupil-sparing, fatigable ptosis and diplopia without long-tract or other brainstem signs, with positive AChR antibodies, do not need brain MRI (Jacob 2025 ABN guidance).
No cardiac symptom or sign; echocardiography is not part of the MG work-up.
No palpitations, syncope or arrhythmia; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, AChR antibody-positive, generalized (MGFA Class IIb), new onset after recent Guillain-Barré syndrome (sequential/concurrent autoimmunity)

differential.key_features: Leg strength and sensory symptoms keep improving and repeat conduction studies are better than 4 weeks ago; the new deficits are fatigable ocular and bulbar signs with a facial RNS decrement and positive AChR antibodies.
No new ascending or sensory deterioration, and conduction studies are improving rather than worsening after the GBS illness.

differential.diagnosis: Miller Fisher syndrome or GBS with ophthalmoplegia (anti-GQ1b)
differential.key_features: Anti-GQ1b negative, no ataxia, and the ptosis and diplopia fluctuate and fatigue; the low reflexes are residual from the GBS illness.
Pupils spared, no long-tract or other brainstem signs, fluctuating fatigable pattern with a junctional cause shown.
Objective fatigable ptosis, positive ice-pack test, RNS decrement and AChR antibodies.

key_clinical_evidence: New fatigable ptosis, diplopia, jaw fatigue and nasal speech with diurnal variation appeared while the GBS deficits were improving; GBS had no cranial involvement.
Positive ice-pack test on the left (MRD1 +2.5 mm).
Anti-AChR binding 2.1 nmol/L with elevated blocking and modulating antibodies establishes AChR-positive MG; anti-GQ1b is negative.
RNS shows a 13% nasalis decrement with post-activation exhaustion and no facilitation; the residual demyelinating features are improving, which argues against a GBS relapse.
FVC 57% predicted (31.3 mL/kg) with a 12% supine fall and MIP -46 cmH2O: reduced reserve that calls for monitored care and rapid therapy.
Mediastinal CT shows thymic hyperplasia without thymoma; thymectomy is indicated per MGTX once he is stable.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Fatigable ptosis and diplopia are not features of GBS; AChR antibodies and the RNS decrement establish a new MG, and the improving conduction studies argue against a relapse.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute new ocular symptoms to GBS recurrence and treat empirically without re-investigating.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Anti-GQ1b absence is reassuring against MFS but does not address MG; AChR testing is the diagnostic step.

sequence_constraints.reason: AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).
Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).

findings.description: Diffusely enlarged thymus with preserved arrowhead shape and smooth margins; no focal nodule, calcification or cystic change.
findings.size: Left lobe 1.7 cm thick, right lobe 1.3 cm

body_imaging.impression: CT chest with contrast: 1. Diffuse thymic enlargement with preserved shape and homogeneous attenuation, most consistent with thymic hyperplasia; no discrete mass to suggest thymoma. 2. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear.

labs.interpretation: Anti-AChR binding 2.1 nmol/L, blocking 28% and modulating 42%, all elevated; anti-MuSK and anti-GQ1b IgG not detected. CBC, BMP and thyroid function within reference ranges. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in a subset of patients with disorders of neuromuscular transmission; clinical correlation recommended.

results.finding: Pyridostigmine is the initial symptomatic treatment; IVIG or plasma exchange is used for severe or rapidly worsening weakness, including bulbar weakness, and before thymectomy in patients with significant bulbar or respiratory weakness.
results.source: Sanders DB et al. Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al. Neurology 2021;96:114-122

results.finding: Thymectomy improved clinical outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
results.source: Wolfe GI et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522

myasthenia gravis diagnosis and manageme.summary: Consensus guidance (Sanders DB et al., Neurology 2016;87:419-425; update Narayanaswami P et al., Neurology 2021;96:114-122) recommends AChR antibody testing first, MuSK testing when AChR antibodies are absent, and electrodiagnostic confirmation by repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fibre EMG. Chest CT or MRI is recommended in all patients to detect thymoma. In the MGTX trial (Wolfe GI et al., N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522) thymectomy improved outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.

patient.chief_complaint: New bilateral ptosis and diplopia 4 weeks after 'Guillain-Barré syndrome' hospitalization

past_medical_history: Hospitalized 4 weeks ago for acute ascending weakness (initially thought to be Guillain-Barré syndrome, discharged with diagnosis of mild GBS)

patient.history_present_illness: A 42-year-old man was re-admitted to neurology after developing new bilateral ptosis and diplopia following a hospitalization 4 weeks ago for acute ascending weakness attributed to Guillain-Barré syndrome. During the prior admission, he had presented with ascending leg weakness over 5 days, areflexia, and mild sensory symptoms. CSF showed a protein of 58 mg/dL with 2 cells/uL, nerve conduction studies reportedly showed mild demyelinating features, and he received a 5-day course of IVIG with partial improvement in leg strength. He was discharged with mild residual leg weakness and sensory symptoms on gabapentin; enoxaparin prophylaxis was stopped at discharge. Over the 2 weeks following discharge, he developed new bilateral eyelid drooping and double vision, which had not been present during his initial presentation or hospitalization; his prior illness had no cranial nerve involvement. The new symptoms have a clear diurnal variation: worse at the end of the day, significantly better after sleep. He also reports jaw fatigue during meals. His girlfriend has noticed his voice becomes nasal after prolonged conversations. He denies breathlessness, dysphagia, or return of the ascending leg weakness, and his leg strength and sensory symptoms continue to improve. He was readmitted for evaluation.

neurological_exam.additional: No dysphagia currently. Speech becomes nasal and slurred after about 3 minutes of sustained speech.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: New bilateral ptosis over the past 2 weeks, left greater than right. Fatigable ptosis on sustained upgaze (left lid covers the pupil at 40 seconds). New horizontal diplopia on rightward gaze. Pupils equal, reactive. Mild facial weakness bilaterally. Dysarthria after 3 minutes of sustained speech.
neurological_exam.motor: Proximal upper extremity 4/5. Proximal lower extremity 4/5, both declining with repeated testing. Distal 5/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Hyporeflexia 1+ throughout (residual from GBS). Plantar downgoing.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild stocking decrease to light touch bilaterally (residual GBS sensory involvement).

physical_exam.general: Weight 83.0 kg, height 176 cm. Well appearing, speaking full sentences, no respiratory distress.
